sources.excerpt: Wampler Pedals Low Blow Review: Deep, Dynamic Bass Boost Pedal Analysis | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Wampler Pedals Low Blow Review: Deep, Dynamic Bass Boost Pedal Analysis By liam-carter June 13, 2026 Wampler Pedals Low Blow Review The Wampler Low Blow is a high-headroom, transparent bass-boost pedal designed for players who need low-end reinforcement without muddiness or loss of clarity—especially guitarists using single-coils, low-output pickups, or extended-range instruments, and bassists seeking subtle foundational lift rather than distortion or overdrive. It delivers a focused +12 dB boost centered at 80 Hz with fully variable control over frequency (40–160 Hz), gain (+0 to +12 dB), and blend (0–100% wet/dry). Unlike many ‘bass boosters,’ it preserves transients and articulation, making it viable for clean rhythm work, dynamic lead passages, and studio layering. This Wampler Pedals Low Blow review confirms it excels where precision matters most—but it’s not a substitute for EQ shaping or a dedicated sub-octave effect. Its value lies in surgical low-end reinforcement, not tonal transformation. About Wampler Pedals Low Blow Review: Product Background Released in 2019, the Low Blow emerged from Wampler Pedals’ ongoing focus on transparent, high-fidelity signal enhancement tools. Founded by Brian Wampler in 2007, the company has built its reputation on boutique analog circuitry, meticulous component selection, and no-compromise build quality—initially known for overdrives like the Pinnacle and Ego, later expanding into modulation, delay, and utility pedals. The Low Blow was conceived as a response to guitarist and bassist requests for a clean, non-coloring low-frequency amplifier—not a ‘fat’ or ‘woofy’ booster, but a calibrated tool for restoring low-end lost through pedalboards, long cable runs, or FRFR systems. It sits outside Wampler’s core overdrive lineup and instead belongs to their growing category of ‘enhancement utilities’: devices that address specific technical gaps in signal chains without altering core tone identity. First Impressions: Build Quality, Setup, and Design Unboxing reveals a standard Wampler 4.5" × 2.5" aluminum enclosure—matte black anodized finish, laser-etched labeling, and recessed knobs with soft-touch rubber caps. The footswitch is a sealed, momentary, true-bypass switch with tactile feedback and quiet operation (no audible click during engagement). All controls are top-mounted: Frequency (40–160 Hz), Gain (0–12 dB), and Blend (0–100%). A single 9 V DC input accepts center-negative power only—no battery option. The internal layout uses discrete op-amps (TI OPA2134 dual) and film capacitors throughout, consistent with Wampler’s stated design philosophy of transparency and headroom 1 . No LEDs blink or pulse—the pedal operates silently when bypassed, and the signal path remains fully analog with no digital processing. Setup requires no calibration or firmware updates; simply plug in, set controls to noon for baseline testing, and adjust incrementally. Detailed Specifications Below is the complete specification set, interpreted with practical context for musicians: Power Requirement: 9 V DC, center-negative, 30 mA minimum (standard Boss-style adapter) Input Impedance: 1 MΩ — compatible with passive and active pickups without loading issues Output Impedance: 100 Ω — low enough to drive long cables or complex pedalboard loops without high-frequency roll-off Frequency Range: Continuously variable from 40 Hz to 160 Hz — covers fundamental bass notes (E1=41 Hz, A1=55 Hz) up through lower-mid ‘body’ frequencies (G2=98 Hz, D3=147 Hz) Boost Range: 0 to +12 dB — measured at peak frequency; linear taper ensures precise adjustment, especially below +6 dB Blend Control: 0–100% parallel mix — enables subtle ‘just a touch’ reinforcement or full wet signal for dramatic low-end emphasis True Bypass: Mechanical relay-based switching with LED i
